Generate Bayesian coverage model object

Source: R/3_baye_model.R
generate_bayes_model.Rd

Fits a Bayesian coverage model for one indicator, combining the survey estimates and the routine (DHIS2) coverage in coverage_data with the yearly data quality score in overall_score. The model is national or sub-national (admin level 1), following the admin level of coverage_data.

Usage

generate_bayes_model(
  coverage_data,
  overall_score,
  indicator = c("anc4", "anc_1trimester", "ideliv", "measles1", "penta3"),
  denominator = c("anc1", "dhis2", "penta1", "penta1derived", "anc1derived"),
  keep_samples = FALSE
)

Arguments

coverage_data

Survey data frame of class 'cd_coverage'.

overall_score

DHIS2 data frame of class 'cd_overall_score'.

indicator

Indicator character code (e.g., 'anc4', 'penta3').

denominator

The denominator type to use from DHIS2 (e.g., 'penta1', 'dhis2').

keep_samples

Whether the model keeps the sampler's draws and the compiled Stan model (samples, stan_model). Default FALSE: the charts and bayes_model_estimates() read the summary of the draws, which is kept either way, and a model without the draws is much smaller (tens to hundreds of KB instead of tens of MB), so it is quicker to save and to pass between processes.

Value

An object of class cd_bayes_model: the fitted model returned by bayescoveragedeploy::fit_local_model() (a list, with its posteriors summary), without samples and stan_model unless keep_samples = TRUE. It carries the attributes indicator, model_indicator (the name the model uses for the indicator), iso and is_national.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# needs the Bayesian model packages (see cd_bayes_packages_missing()); a fit takes minutes
path <- system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core")
cache <- load_cache_data(path)
cache$set_national_estimates(list(sbr = 0.02))
cache$adjust_data()

model <- generate_bayes_model(
  coverage_data = cache$calculate_coverage("national"),
  overall_score = cache$overall_score,
  indicator = "penta3",
  denominator = "penta1"
)
bayes_model_estimates(model)
plot(model)
} # }
